auditor.report:
Batch: 48 runs. 43 accepted, 5 declined (r12, r19, r23, r36, r45; all failed closure). No runs used a remedy, the width-free ratio or a roll-back.
Flagged (2), reason summary_outlier: r31 (control) and r34 (mannitol then control). Their largest flank differences are -99.8 and -105.4 %/h, about 3 MAD from the batch median of 14.9 %/h and about three times the root's own centre REGR peak. r34's sits at 2042 µm, past its growth zone. Their centre peak, peak position and growth-zone length are normal. Closure passed on both.
Cleared (41): every other accepted run. Closure passed on all of them, and their profile shapes match the batch.
What the flagged runs share: a normal centre profile, but a flank-difference (curvature-rate) signal much larger than the centre strain rate. Plane sections is not a gate for these real movies, so nothing else checks that signal.
Medians by condition for accepted runs (REGR peak, peak position, growth-zone length):
- Control (n=14): about 39 %/h, 579 µm, 757 µm
- Mannitol (n=9): about 38 %/h, 705 µm, 653 µm
- Mannitol then control (n=17): about 36 %/h, 663 µm, 874 µm
- Mannitol then mannitol (n=3: r13, r14, r24): about 9–10 %/h, peak at 1610–1894 µm, growth zone 21–63 µm. This is a nearly arrested profile with passing closure, consistent across all three roots. It is reported as a result of the condition, not a measurement fault.
Flank differences take both signs in every condition. Faster roots (r15, r20, r27, with REGR peaks of 54–55 %/h) have a normal profile shape.
